chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Tahir ibn Hatim during a state of orthodoxy,

that he wrote to the man (the Imam): 'What is it without which the recognition of the Creator would be deficient?' So he wrote to him: '(God) has always been Knowing, Hearing, and Seeing, and He is the Doer of whatever He wills.'

And Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) was asked about that without which the recognition of the Creator would be deficient, so he said: 'Nothing is like Him, nor does anything resemble Him. He has always been Knowing, Hearing, Seeing.'

key_terms.اسْتِقَامَة: Uprightness/orthodoxy — a rijal term meaning the narrator held correct beliefs at that time
key_terms.الْفَعَّالُ لِمَا يُرِيدُ: The Doer of what He wills — affirms divine omnipotence and absolute will
key_terms.لَمْ يَزَلْ: Has not ceased / has always been — denotes God's eternal attribute without beginning
key_terms.لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِ شَيْءٌ: Nothing is like Him — the core theological principle of divine transcendence (tanzih), quoting Quran 42:11
key_terms.مَعْرِفَةُ الْخَالِقِ: Recognition/knowledge of the Creator — the theological discipline of knowing God's attributes

ai.seo_question: What are the minimum attributes necessary for recognizing the Creator according to the Imams?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a two-part theological exchange about the minimum necessary attributes for recognizing God (the Creator). First, Tahir ibn Hatim wrote to the Imam asking what is indispensable for recognizing God, and the Imam replied that God has eternally been Knowing, Hearing, and Seeing — and that He is the Doer of whatever He wills. Second, when Imam Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) was independently asked the same question, he declared the doctrine of God's absolute incomparability: nothing is like Him, nothing resembles Him, and He has always been Knowing, Hearing, and Seeing. The phrase 'during a state of orthodoxy' (fi hal istiqamatih) qualifies Tahir ibn Hatim, indicating that this narration was transmitted while he held correct beliefs, which was a standard rijal criterion for evaluating a narrator's reliability.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Tahir Bin Hatim during a state of normality,

‘He wrote to the man<sup>asws</sup> (Imam Reza<sup>asws</sup>), ‘What is that without which the recognition of the Creator would be deficient?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> wrote to him: ‘(It is that) He<sup>azwj</sup> does not cease to be Knowing, and Hearing, and Seeing, and He<sup>azwj</sup> Does whatever He<sup>azwj</sup> so Desires to.

And Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> was asked about that without which the recognition of the Creator would be deficient, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘(It is that) There is nothing like Him<sup>azwj</sup> nor does anything resemble Him<sup>azwj</sup>. He does not Cease to be Knowing, Hearing, Seeing’’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Tahir ibn Hatam when he was normal

and wrote to the man (meaning thereby Imam abul Hassan al-Rida (a.s.). “What is it that without which one’s acknowledgement of the existence of Allah can not be considered sufficient?” In answer the Imam (a.s.) replied, “That He is All-knowing, All-hearing All-awareness and that He acts as He wills.”

Imam abu Ja‘far (a.s.) was asked about the minimum required degree of knowledge about Allah without which an acknowledgement would not be considered sufficient. The Imam (a.s.) said, “There is nothing similar to or like Him. He is All-knowing, All-hearing and All-awareness.”
